questions.question: Q: Why is interactivity the key difference between video games and other media forms?

points.text: In video games, the player makes choices that directly affect the experience — where to go, what to do, how to respond. Unlike film or TV where the audience passively watches a fixed narrative, games give players agency. This creates personal investment and emotional engagement that passive media cannot replicate.

questions.question: Q: How are video games regulated in the UK?

points.text: Video games are classified by PEGI (Pan European Game Information), which assigns age ratings (3, 7, 12, 16, 18) and content descriptors (violence, fear, drugs, bad language). PEGI ratings are legally enforceable in the UK — it is illegal to sell an 18-rated game to someone under 18. The VSC Rating Board enforces PEGI in the UK.

questions.question: Q: Evaluate the representation of gender in video games.

points.text: Historically, games have underrepresented and stereotyped women — male protagonists dominate, female characters are often sexualised or serve as 'damsels in distress'. markScheme.exemplarAnswer: Video games have historically stereotyped social groups, but contemporary games increasingly offer complex, diverse representations. Gender representation has been particularly problematic. Female characters have been underrepresented as protagonists and overrepresented as sexualised objects or passive supporting characters. The 'male gaze' (Mulvey) is evident in character design that emphasises physical attractiveness over personality or agency. However, recent games feature strong female protagonists (e.g. Aloy in Horizon, Ellie in The Last of Us) who drive the narrative and are not defined by their appearance. Ethnic representation also has a troubled history. Non-white characters have been marginalised, stereotyped, or absent. When included, they are often supporting characters or villains. Recent progress includes more diverse leads, but the industry's workforce remains predominantly white and male, affecting whose stories are told. LGBTQ+ representation is growing but still limited. Some AAA games now include LGBTQ+ characters and romance options, but they remain a small proportion of all characters. Indie games have been more progressive in representing diverse sexualities and gender identities. Age and disability representation remains particularly poor. Elderly and disabled characters are rare, and when present, often serve as narrative devices rather than fully developed characters. Overall, while video game representations are improving, they lag behind other media
